newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta strength worrisome, Catalan leader says.
newsitem.headline: Peseta strength worrisome, Catalan leader says.

text.p: A leader of the Catalan coalition which holds the balance of power in Spain expressed concern on Friday over the economic impact of the peseta's recent strength.
"The strength of the peseta is worrying because it influences the competitiveness of our economy," Joaquin Molins of Catalonia's ruling coalition Convergencia i Unio (CiU) told state radio.
Around 0950 GMT the peseta was trading at around 83.41/44 per mark against a Thursday close of 83.48/49.
The Bank of Spain on Thursday cut its key money market rate by 25 basis points to 6.00 percent, but this had little effect on the Spanish currency.
Traders said they had not seen the central bank intervening in the market since last Friday, when the peseta broke trough the key 84.00 per mark barrier.
